title: Confluence
briefing: Meadow Pharma is trending up and about to pull back; Harborline Shipping keeps flashing "oversold" on the way down. Look for reasons that agree, not just one loud signal.
objective: Combine trend, price level and indicator before entering, and plan the stop.
debrief: Meadow Pharma stayed above its rising average. The patent scare on day 13 pulled it back to the average and old support, RSI dipped and turned up, and the patent ruling on day 20 restarted the trend: three independent reasons lined up. Harborline looked "oversold" again and again, but the falling freight rates on day 8 and the dividend cut on day 18 kept it sliding. A disciplined player bought the pullback with a stop and ignored the falling knife.

news.headline: Container shipping rates fall for a fifth week
news.body: Too many ships are chasing too little cargo, pushing prices down.

news.headline: Rival files a competing patent; Meadow Pharma dips
news.body: A competitor claims part of Meadow's allergy medicine. Meadow says the claim has no merit.

news.headline: Harborline halves its dividend
news.body: The company is saving cash while shipping rates stay low.

news.headline: Patent office sides with Meadow Pharma
news.body: The rival's claim was rejected; Meadow keeps its patent.

basic.text: Buy Meadow Pharma on the pullback to its rising average, days 13 to 18
Protect your entry with a stop-loss

bonus.text: Keep Harborline at or under 10% of your portfolio: oversold in a downtrend is not a setup
